claims.explanation: The selective killing pattern is best explained by TP53 loss-of-function, which sensitizes cells to AM-92016, possibly because p53-deficient cells are less able to arrest and repair damage caused by potassium-channel blockade and downstream stress. The drug's weak NMDA-receptor (GRIN1) and calcium-channel-related transcriptional signature suggests that TP53-mutant lines with additional RTK/RAS or PI3K pathway alterations may be particularly vulnerable, while intact p53 signaling is protective.

Co-occurs with TP53 mutation in sensitive melanoma and other lines; cell-cycle checkpoint loss

Observed in sensitive NSCLC lines (HCC4006, HCC95, NCIH1650, KYSE270)
Observed in several sensitive lines (GSU, OV7, SNU410) but also in resistant lines, so weaker
Observed in sensitive ZR751 and KALS1; PI3K/AKT pathway activation may increase dependence on K+ channels
Observed in sensitive LOXIMVI and KALS1; RAS pathway activation
Observed in sensitive GSU and OV7; cell-cycle deregulation
Observed in sensitive OV7 and KYSE270; chromatin remodeling loss
Observed in sensitive LOXIMVI and KU1919; chromatin remodeling loss
Annotated target; NMDA receptor activity may protect via calcium signaling, and its blockade could contribute to selective toxicity
Drug is a delayed rectifier K+ channel blocker; hERG expression may mediate sensitivity or resistance
